implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: define a SecurityContext value holding the authenticated principal plus the attributes guards need (roles or scopes, tenant, authentication method), keep it immutable once bound, and let exactly one component - the authentication boundary - create and bind it. Expose a single typed accessor to consumers and make every guard treat an absent context as unauthenticated; unbind deterministically when the unit of work ends, because the holder's granularity (thread, task, request, explicit parameter) determines both the propagation policy and the leak risk. Add the holder only where an ambient read is genuinely required: an explicit context parameter is always the safer default, and a holder without a matching unbind is a defect waiting for the first pooled execution unit.
code_sketch:
# boundary, after verification succeeded
ctx = SecurityContext(principal, tenant, method)
bind(ctx)
try:
    handle(request)          # guards call current_context() and deny when absent
finally:
    unbind()                 # never leave a principal for the next unit of work
pitfalls: A holder without a deterministic unbind is a leak waiting for the first pooled execution unit.
The holder's granularity (thread, task, request, explicit parameter) must match the runtime's execution unit, or guards read a binding that belongs to someone else.
Only the boundary may create a context; consumers that can also write it destroy the single-source-of-truth property.

Inheritable thread-locals copy the binding when a thread is CREATED, not when a task is submitted: a pool worker that happens to be created while request A runs keeps A's principal for every later task it serves, so inheritance into shared pools must be replaced by per-task capture-and-restore wrappers.
